subject.title: feat(fleet): multi-tenant hosting via openclaw fleet cell supervisor

question: Should OpenClaw core own `openclaw fleet` as the supported multi-tenant isolation and lifecycle boundary?
rationale: The PR creates a durable security, persistence, upgrade, and operator-facing CLI contract; patch correctness alone cannot decide whether core should own that product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor core Fleet
options.body: Approve core ownership after all blocking defects, conflicts, and Linux Docker/Podman proof are resolved.

options.title: Keep orchestration external
options.body: Retain the one-cell-per-tenant security guidance but move lifecycle supervision to an external package or deployment tool.

options.title: Pause the design
options.body: Hold the implementation while maintainers narrow the threat model, supported platforms, and long-term compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core Fleet
recommendation.body: Approve core ownership after all blocking defects, conflicts, and Linux Docker/Podman proof are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged shared-state work and authorship of the linked design make this the strongest individual routing candidate, with security-owner review also required.
